title: Grill — harness stacks fix round + improvements
summary:
You already decided the big ones in chat: **fix review items 1–22 and every UX gap**, **remove the transcript cap**, and **add** mirror provenance, a per-stack swap history, per-member quota in the Stacks list and a *switch to next account now* action. Returning to the primary after a reset stays **out of scope**.

What's left are the decisions the build would otherwise make silently. **Four blocking** ones shape the plan: how *switch now* behaves on a live run, how the swap history is stored and kept, how a per-model Codex limit is scoped, and how far mirror backups/restore go. Then a few that shape parts of it, and a confirm list of defaults I'd bet on (one click each).

proven.text: **Claude's `file-history/` is keyed by session id** (`~/.claude/file-history/<sessionId>/<hash>@vN`), so item 17 can copy `/rewind` checkpoints alongside the transcript by sid.

**Finding the source transcript by scanning `projects/*/<sid>.jsonl`** fixes long worktree paths: Claude hashes project-dir names over 200 chars with an unknown input, but copying to the source's own dir name lets the backup's Claude compute the same name from the same cwd.

**Live accounts can already be continued mid-turn**: the limit settlement (`handleHarnessLimitSettlement` → `executeStackSwap` → `spawnSwapContinuation`) copies the session and resumes on the next account. *Switch now* can reuse it with a manual trigger that does **not** cool the account or mark it tried.

**Quota display needs no new connection**: the webview already holds every `HarnessQuota` snapshot in `App.tsx` (seeded from `GET /usage`, kept live by the `harness_usage` app event). The CLI can read `GET /usage` (CLI scope). The force-refresh route stays desktop-only on purpose (it can trigger a cross-app Cursor database read).

proven: **Nothing persists swap events today**: only the successor run's `origin`, a status-line divider and the latest `lastMove` (cleared by the next automatic swap). The history needs a new table (migration 087).
**Codex is not wired for e2e** (`e2e/fixtures.ts` sets only the Claude fake driver). Adding `AGETOR_CODEX_DRIVER=fake` to the fixture is part of the requested Codex-stack e2e.

sections.title: Blocking — these change the plan's shape

questions.title: What should "Switch to next account now" do while the task's run is live?
questions.why: Decides whether this is a small route over the existing idle switch, or a new interrupt path into the swap settlement.
questions.context:
Today a same-stack account change is refused while a run is live (409 "stop the run before switching accounts") because the switch copies the transcript and drops the REPL. The limit settlement already knows how to stop a live turn, copy the conversation and resume it on the next account with a hidden continuation prompt. The obvious use case for *switch now* is an account that is slow, degraded or about to run out mid-turn.

In every option a task held by running background agents is refused (409), as today, and the switch never cools the old account or marks it tried.

options.label: Interrupt and continue on the next account
options.description: Stops the live turn and runs the swap: copy the conversation, resume on the next usable account, divider "Switched to X — continuing this conversation".
options.consequence: Reuses the swap settlement with a manual trigger. Any in-flight tool call is cut off (the same accepted risk as a limit swap).

options.label: Switch after the current turn ends
options.description: Records the request; when the turn settles successfully the task moves to the next account before the next message.
options.consequence: No interrupted tool work, but it doesn't help with an account that is stuck or slow now.

options.label: Only when idle
options.description: Refused (409) while a run is live; the button is disabled with a hint.
options.consequence: Smallest change; the user must Stop first.

recommendation.reason: It's the case the button exists for, and the swap machinery already handles a mid-turn move safely.

questions.title: How should the per-stack swap history be stored and how long is it kept?
questions.why: A migration adds the table; its foreign keys decide what survives task and stack deletes.
questions.context: Proposed table `harness_swap_events` (migration 087): stack id, task id + task title (denormalized), from/to account ids and labels, trigger, reason, source, provider reset time, old/new run ids, continuation kind (transferred/restarted), timestamp. No foreign key to `harnesses` (repo rule, migration 085). Labels are stored so a deleted account still reads by name.

options.label: Kept with the stack, capped per stack
options.description: Survives task delete/archive and account delete; removed when the stack is deleted; oldest rows pruned past a cap (next question).
options.consequence: A history answers "how often does this stack fail over?" even after tasks are cleaned up.

options.label: Deleted with its task
options.description: FK to `tasks` with ON DELETE CASCADE; removed with the stack too.
options.consequence: History shrinks as tasks are deleted; no cap needed.

options.label: Kept forever, even after stack delete
options.description: Shown as "deleted stack" in the CLI.
options.consequence: Unbounded growth; needs a separate cleanup command later.

recommendation.reason: The history is about the stack's accounts, not the tasks, and a cap keeps it bounded without a new cleanup feature.

questions.title: How many swap events to keep per stack before pruning the oldest?

recommendation.reason: Months of heavy use at a few swaps a day, and a cheap indexed delete.

questions.title: Which events go into the swap history?
questions.why: Each one is a write point in a different move path (six exist).

options.label: Limit swaps
options.description: A provider limit moved a live task to the next account.

options.label: Manual switches
options.description: Same-stack account change from the picker/CLI, and *switch now*.

options.label: Moves off an unusable account
options.description: Run/message found the account removed, disabled or logged out and moved on.

options.label: Automatic retries after a reset
options.description: Including a retry that stays on the same account.

options.label: Blocked outcomes
options.description: "Stack out of quota" / "no usable account" — no move happened, but the stack ran out.

options.label: Swaps completed at boot
options.description: A switch the core finished after a restart.

recommendation.reason: A history that omits the blocked and retry rows can't explain why a task waited.

questions.title: Codex "You've hit your usage limit for <model>" — how should a per-model limit be scoped?
questions.why: Decides whether `harness_limit_state` gains a model column (migration) and whether selection checks cooldowns per model.
questions.context: Today it is classified as an account-wide quota, so one task on a heavy model cools the account for every task on every model until the reset (review item 11).

options.label: Cool the account for that model only
options.description: `harness_limit_state` gains a `model` column (null = whole account). Selection skips a member only for tasks on that model; the UI says "cooling for gpt-… until …".

options.label: Move this task only, no cooldown
options.description: The account is marked tried for this task's lap; other tasks keep using it.
options.consequence: No migration; other tasks on the same model will each hit the limit once.

recommendation.reason: It's the only option that stops every task on that model from re-hitting the limit, and it costs one nullable column.

questions.title: Mirror provenance: what happens to a backup's own files and keys the mirror overwrites?
questions.why: Decides the backup store's size, retention and whether a restore surface is built.
questions.context: Provenance (DB table, migration 087) records every file/key the mirror wrote, with a hash. The first time the mirror would replace something the backup already had (its own `CLAUDE.md`, hooks, a skill), the original is saved under `<data dir>/mirror-backups/<account>/…` (0600, outside every account root). Deletion propagation only removes what the mirror wrote **and** the backup hasn't edited since; never a pre-existing original.

options.label: Back up everything overwritten + a Restore action
options.description: Merged files, single files and tree files. Settings → Stacks and `agetor harness stack restore <stack> <account>` put the originals back (and drop provenance for them).
options.consequence: Largest: a restore route, UI and CLI command. Plugin trees can make the store big.

options.label: Back up everything overwritten; recovery by hand
options.description: The preview and the warning name the backup folder; no restore command.
options.consequence: No restore surface to build or test.

options.label: Back up merged and single files only
options.description: settings.json, .claude.json, config.toml, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; tree files that pre-existed are left alone instead of overwritten.
options.consequence: Small store; a pre-existing skill with the same name is no longer replaced (behavior change).

recommendation.reason: You prefer the complete path, and a backup nobody can restore from the app is easy to forget exists.

sections.title: Shape — these change part of the plan

questions.title: When does the save-time mirror preview appear?
questions.why: The preview doubles as the confirm the review asked for before a full-mode mirror overwrites backups.
questions.context: A dry run returns the planned changes per backup: files added/updated/removed, settings keys changed (secret-shaped values redacted), and what would be backed up first.

options.label: Before every mirror-relevant save
options.description: Any change to members, order, kind or mirror mode shows the preview; Save applies it. A preview with no changes skips the dialog.

options.label: Only when something on a backup would be overwritten or removed
options.description: Pure additions save without a dialog.

options.label: On demand only
options.description: A "Preview mirror" button; Save never asks.
options.consequence: Doesn't close the review's "overwrites without asking" gap.

recommendation.reason: It asks exactly when something the user had could change, and stays out of the way otherwise.

questions.title: What does "Clear cooldown" do?
questions.context: A cooldown is account-global (`harness_limit_state`). Today only a successful turn or the reset clears it; a manual Run forces the account for that task only.

options.label: Delete the account's cooldown for every task
options.description: New `DELETE /harnesses/:id/limit-state` (desktop + CLI); the confirm warns the provider may still refuse.
options.consequence: One route, a button in Settings and `agetor harness cooldown clear <account>`.

options.label: Force it for one task only
options.description: Like Run now; the account stays cooling for others.

recommendation.reason: The gap is a false match locking an account everywhere; per-task forcing already exists as Run now.

questions.title: Show the provider's own limit message next to a cooling account?
questions.context: `harness_limit_state` stores `reason`, `source` and the provider `message` (e.g. "You've hit your usage limit… try again at 3:00 PM"). It is third-party text: escaped in the CLI, rendered as plain text in the webview.

options.label: Reason + message (message in a tooltip/detail line)
Normalized reason only (usage limit / rate limit / out of credits)

recommendation.reason: The raw message is what tells you whether it was a false match.

questions.title: The automatic retry waits at least 10 s (hard-coded). May the e2e shorten it with an env override?

options.label: Yes — `AGETOR_HARNESS_RETRY_MIN_MS`, honored only under NODE_ENV=test or the e2e backend flag
options.consequence: Countdown/Run-now/retry e2e run in ~1 s each.

options.label: No — the e2e waits the real 10 s
options.consequence: Slower suite, no new env var.

recommendation.reason: Same pattern as the other test-only seams (AGETOR_OPENCODE_SERVER_HOST).

questions.title: How should this ship?
questions.context: Rough size: well over 5,000 changed lines across core, CLI, webview, two migrations' worth of tables and docs.

options.label: One branch, a commit per wave; you open the PR
options.description: Branch `fix/harness-stacks-fix-round`, nothing pushed.

options.label: A stack of branches
options.description: 1) core bug fixes, 2) mirror fixes + provenance, 3) history/quota/switch-now + surfaces.

recommendation.reason: Your recent features shipped as one PR, and the waves already give reviewable commits.

sections.title: Confirm or override — defaults I'd use

questions.title: A manual switch (picker, CLI, switch now) never cools the old account and never marks it tried

recommendation.value: Confirmed: only a provider limit cools an account; a manual move just picks the next usable member.
recommendation.reason: Cooling on a user's choice would lock a healthy account for 10 minutes.

questions.title: Switch now with no other usable account is refused up front, before anything is stopped

recommendation.value: 409 with the per-member reasons (cooling until …, logged out, …); the live run keeps going.
recommendation.reason: Killing a turn and then discovering there's nowhere to go is the worst outcome.

questions.title: A file/key the mirror wrote and the backup later edited is never removed by deletion propagation

recommendation.value: Kept, with a warning naming it; provenance for it is dropped.
recommendation.reason: The edit is the backup's own work now.

questions.title: Switching full → safe mirror stops owning hooks/permissions but leaves the backup's current values in place

recommendation.value: Provenance rows for keys safe mode no longer mirrors are dropped; nothing on the backup is deleted.
recommendation.reason: Safe mode is about not running the primary's commands, not about wiping the backup.

questions.title: Stack edits carry the `updatedAt` they were based on; a mismatch answers 409

recommendation.value: Webview: toast "This stack changed elsewhere — reloaded", the editor reloads with the current stack. CLI: `stack edit` always sends the updatedAt it just fetched; a 409 says to re-run.
recommendation.reason: Silent last-write-wins is what drops members today.

questions.title: CLI stack references resolve as exact id → exact label → unique id prefix

recommendation.value: A label shared by two stacks is an error listing both ids, like an ambiguous task prefix.
recommendation.reason: Same rules as task refs (`src/cli/resolve.ts`).

questions.title: The RunPanel account picker keeps outside-stack accounts selectable, grouped and labelled

recommendation.value: Two groups: "This stack — keeps the conversation" (with n/m and cooling marks) and "Other accounts — starts a fresh session". The select shows a spinner and stays disabled while a switch copies.
recommendation.reason: Cross-account moves are legitimate; they just need to say what they do.

questions.title: Per-member quota shows the stored snapshot with its age; past 20 minutes it's marked stale

recommendation.value: Webview: compact meter per member (5h / weekly), from the app's usage map. CLI `stack ls/show`: the same from GET /usage. No force refresh from the CLI.
recommendation.reason: 20 min is the selection's own staleness threshold.

questions.title: A quota snapshot counts as exhausted when any blocking window (Claude 5h/weekly, Codex session/weekly) is at 100% and no credits meter has headroom; its reset is the latest exhausted window's

recommendation.reason: Requiring every meter at 100% never fires in practice.

questions.title: AWS/Azure/Vertex/Google credentials in the process env count as Claude login evidence only with a provider selector (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/VERTEX/FOUNDRY), and then as "unknown"

recommendation.reason: Without a selector Claude never uses them.
